chunks: With this chain of transmission, from Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā, from Abū Jaʿfar, from his father, from Zurʿah, from Samāʿah, who said:

I asked him about the amount of water that suffices for ghusl, and he said: “The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم performed ghusl with one ṣāʿ, and performed wudu (ablution) with one mudd. The ṣāʿ in his time was five arṭāl, and the mudd was the measure of one riṭl and three uqiyyahs.”

key_terms.أَرْطَالٍ: plural of riṭl, a weight or volume measure used to explain the ṣāʿ
key_terms.أَوَاقٍ: plural of uqiyyah, a unit of measure used to define the mudd
key_terms.الْغُسْلِ: ritual bath requiring a sufficient amount of water for purification
key_terms.صَاعٍ: a prophetic measure of volume used here for ghusl
key_terms.مُدٍّ: a smaller prophetic measure of volume used here for wudu (ablution)

ai.seo_question: How much water is sufficient for ghusl and wudu (ablution) according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith states the amount of water sufficient for ghusl and wudu (ablution), citing the practice of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم. It serves as a jurisprudential proof for moderation in ritual purity and preserves the Prophetic standard of measurement.
